David,
the column "n_images" is a new feature since version 1.2 (see the news file, my bad for not posting about the new version here in the group yet). It will be created regardless of how you set the function arguments. The idea is to give users the number of images in a particular event, which of course if only relevant when minDeltaTime is not 0.

By the same token, the new arguments "eventSummaryColumn" and "eventSummaryFunction" can be used to calculate statistics over the events (e.g. mean ambient temperature, maximum count of indivuduals etc). This is because in the past (when minDeltaTime is not 0) only the metadata of the first image of an event was reported, the rest omitted despite potentially useful information.

As a general note, data frames with heterogeneous columns can be combined with rbindlist from the data.table package. You need to store all data frames in a list first, then call rbindlist. It works like a charm.

Jürgen

Thank you and kind regards,
Jürgen

Hi Michelle,

The issue is that assessTemporalIndependence is an internal and undocumented (i.e., no help file) function in recordTable, which I only provided as a temporary fix for filtering existing record tables in this thread <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/camtrapr/assessTemporalIndependence/camtrapr/WTnkVa0IhUg/CpXT5U54AQAJ> because there is no proper function to filter existing record tables yet. This is why not all arguments from recordTable work in assessTemporalIndependence
Some suggestions though:

- if you took the code for assessTemporalIndependence from the other thread <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/camtrapr/assessTemporalIndependence/camtrapr/WTnkVa0IhUg/CpXT5U54AQAJ> here on the group, it may be a bit dated, has changed in the meantime, and is likely to change more in the future. If you use it, please use the most recent version, which you can access via camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence() or from github <https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/blob/master/camtrapR/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R#L353> (on github may be development version not yet on CRAN, so I'd advise against it).
- to remove the birds in your example, I'd run assessTemporalIndependence without the exclude argument and remove birds afterwards.

records_filter10_min_no_birds <- records_filter10_min [!records_filter10_min$Species %in% "Bird", ]

Please let me know if there's further issues.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,
the issue might be due to Excel. When you open a csv table in Excel and save it, date formats may change. This is because of the automatic date formatting that Excel does and then saves. So depending on your system settings, 2019-12-31 may become 31/12/2019 or something else, and the dateFormat argument in R needs to be changed.

Likewise, the date/time column in record tables may lose their seconds when saved in Excel. The original can be restored with the date and time columns which are provided separately in record tables.

Hence it is good practice to check the date format when loading data into R. Since this is a recurrent issue I'll see if I can find some sort of automatic check if the dateFormat provided by the user fits the data.
Thank you for the feedback and feel free to let me know if there's more issues.
Best regards,
Jürgen
